newsitem.title: USA: Carpenter Technology to acquire Dynamet for $161 million.
newsitem.headline: Carpenter Technology to acquire Dynamet for $161 million.

text.p: Carpenter Technology Corp., a speciality metals maker, said Tuesday it plans to acquire Dynamet Inc., a Washington, Pa.-based manufacturer of titanium bar, wire and powder, for $161 million.
Carpenter said the acquisition price includes $150 million in stock and cash and $11 million of Dynamet debt.
The company said that it will pay for privately held Dynamet with 2.8 million shares of its own shares and $51 million in cash.
Following the news, Reading, Pa.-based Carpenter's stock lost $1 at $35.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dynamet is currently owned by the family of P.C. Rossin, its founder and current chairman and chief executive, and the family of Peter Stephans, the current president and chief operating officer.
After the acquisition, which is expected to be completed in March, Rossin will join Carpenter's board. Stephans will serve as a consultant to the business.
After the acquisition, Stephans also plans to purchase Dynamet's forged products operation in McMurray, Pa., for cash and assumption of debt, for a total of $4 million.
Robert Torcolini, currently vice president of manufacturing operations for Carpenter's steel division, will become president of Dynamet.
Dynamet employs 320 people at its plants in Clearwater, Fla.; Washington, McMurray and Bridgeville, Pa.; and at a warehouse in Stanton, Calif.
